blocks.en: Appendix A Taxonomy and Statistics of RISEBench++
blocks.zh: 附录A RISE Bench++的分类和统计

blocks.en: RISEBench++ comprises 1,000 carefully curated tasks spanning six major reasoning dimensions: temporal, causal, spatial, logical, counterfactual, and hybrid reasoning. As summarized in Table 8 , each dimension is further organized into fine-grained subcategories and task types, covering diverse reasoning scenarios from common-sense and disciplinary knowledge to spatial relations, rule-based deduction, and counterfactual imagination. This hierarchical taxonomy is designed to provide broad and balanced coverage of reasoning capabilities while enabling fine-grained analysis of model performance across different reasoning skills.
blocks.zh: RISE Bench++包含1 000个精心设计的任务,涉及六个主要推理方面:时间、因果关系、空间、逻辑、反事实和混合推理。 如表8所概述,每个维度被进一步划分为细微的子类别和任务类型,涵盖从常识和学科知识到空间关系、基于规则的推算和反事实想象的各种推理情景。 这种分级分类法旨在为推理能力提供广泛而平衡的涵盖范围,同时能够对不同推理技能的模型性能进行精细分析.

blocks.en: Appendix B Generalization Evaluation of RISE-Agent on KRIS-Bench
blocks.zh: 附录B 在KRIS-Bench上评价RISE-代理公司

blocks.en: To further evaluate the generalization ability of RISE-Agent, we conduct additional experiments on KRIS-Bench, which assesses factual, conceptual, and procedural knowledge. As shown in Table 9 , RISE-Agent achieves an overall score of 88.12, outperforming all open-source models and existing agentic methods. Among agentic methods, RISE-Agent obtains the best results across all reported knowledge categories, with particularly strong performance on factual knowledge (89.14) and conceptual knowledge (87.77). It also achieves 97.06 on instruction-following tasks. While the closed-source GPT-Image-2.5 models achieve the highest overall scores on KRIS-Bench, RISE-Agent remains competitive and substantially narrows the gap while relying on an agentic framework. These results indicate that the effectiveness of RISE-Agent transfers well to an additional benchmark with a different evaluation setup, providing further evidence of its generalization capability beyond RISEBench++.
blocks.zh: 为了进一步评价RISE-Agent的通俗化能力,我们对KRIS-Bench进行了更多的实验,对事实、概念和程序知识进行了评估。 如表9所示,RISE-Agent的总得分为88.12分,超越了所有开源模型和现有代理方法. 在代理方法中,RISE-Agent在所有报告的知识类别中获得最佳结果,在事实知识(89.14)和概念知识(87.77)。 它还完成了97.06项指导任务。 虽然封闭源代码GPT-Image-2.5的模型在KRIS-Bench上取得了最高的总分,但RISE-Agent仍然具有竞争力并大大缩小了差距,同时依赖于代理框架. 这些结果表明,RISE-Agent的效能很好地转移到了另一个具有不同评价结构的基准,进一步证明了其在RISE Bench++之外的通化能力.

blocks.en: Appendix C Detailed Performance across Three Evaluation Dimensions
blocks.zh: 附录C 三个评价层面的业绩

blocks.en: Tables 11 and 12 provide a fine-grained breakdown of model performance across different reasoning categories under the three evaluation dimensions, i.e., IR, AC, and VP, for the English and Chinese versions, respectively. Overall, the results reveal substantial variation across both evaluation dimensions and reasoning categories. While many models achieve relatively strong AC and VP scores, IR remains considerably more challenging, particularly for logical and hybrid reasoning. In contrast, temporal, causal, and spatial reasoning generally yield higher IR scores, suggesting that current models handle more explicit structural or relational constraints better than reasoning processes that require multi-step logical composition or the integration of multiple reasoning types. The gap is especially evident among open-source models, where high visual quality or constraint adherence does not necessarily translate into strong reasoning correctness. Importantly, these trends are broadly consistent across the English and Chinese settings, indicating that the observed difficulty is not specific to a particular language. Together, these results highlight the complementary nature of IR, AC, and VP and reinforce the importance of evaluating reasoning-intensive image generation beyond visual quality or instruction compliance alone.
blocks.zh: 表11和表12提供了三个评价维度下不同推理类别模型性能的细微分解,即英语版和中文版的IR,AC和VP. 总体而言,评价结果显示评价层面和推理类别之间有很大差异。 虽然许多模型都取得了相对强大的AC和VP分数,但IR仍然具有相当大的挑战性,特别是对逻辑推理和混合推理而言. 相形之下,时间,因果,和空间推理一般产生更高的IR分数,说明目前的模型处理更明确的结构或关系约束比推理过程要好,因为推理过程需要多步逻辑组成或多步推理类型的融合. 这一差距在开源模型中尤其明显,其中高视觉质量或约束性坚持并不一定转化为强推理正确. 重要的是,这些趋势在英语和汉语背景上大体一致,表明观察到的困难并非特定语言所特有的. 这些结果共同凸显出IR,AC和VP的互补性,并强化了仅评价视觉质量或指令合规性之外的推理密集型图像生成的重要性.

blocks.en: Appendix D Fine-grained Accuracy across Task Types
blocks.zh: 附录D 跨任务类型精确度

blocks.en:
We report task-level accuracy for all evaluated models in Tables 13 – 15 and Tables 16 – 18 for the English and Chinese versions, respectively.
Closed-source models generally achieve higher accuracy across a broad range of task types, particularly those involving physical changes, spatial structures, and counterfactual scenarios. Open-source models show relative strengths in some physical transformation and anomaly editing tasks, but remain weaker on tasks requiring disciplinary knowledge or logical rules. Agentic methods vary substantially, with some performing competitively on knowledge-based and rule-based tasks while others remain weak across many categories. Moreover, even strong models exhibit noticeable variation across individual task types. For example, Nano Banana Pro achieves 100.0% accuracy on Material Transformation but only 25.0% on Chemistry in the English setting, indicating that performance can vary substantially even within the same reasoning category. Logical tasks, especially pattern prediction and other rule-intensive problems, are consistently challenging across all three groups. Similar trends are observed in both English and Chinese, suggesting that these task-level difficulty patterns are largely consistent across languages and may be obscured by aggregate scores.

我们分别在表13 -- -- 15和表16 -- -- 18中报告英文和中文本中所有评价模型的任务级别准确性。
闭源模型一般在一系列广泛的任务类型中,特别是涉及物理变化、空间结构和反事实情景的任务类型中达到更高的精确度。 开源模型在一些物理转换和异常编辑任务中显示出了相对的优势,但在需要学科知识或逻辑规则的任务上仍然较弱. 代理方法大相径庭,有些是在基于知识和基于规则的任务上以竞争性方式执行的,而另一些则在许多类别中仍然薄弱。 此外,即使是强健的模型,也显示出各个任务类型之间的明显差异。 例如纳米香蕉 Pro在材料转化上实现了100.0%的精度,而英语环境中的化学上只有25.0%,这表明即使是在同一推理类中,性能也可能有很大差异. 逻辑任务,特别是模式预测和其他规则密集型问题,在所有三个组别中始终具有挑战性。 在英语和汉语中都观察到了类似的趋势,这表明这些任务级难度模式在语言之间基本一致,可能被总分所掩盖.

blocks.en: Appendix E Score Distributions across Models
blocks.zh: 附录E 各种模型的分数分布

blocks.en: We present the score distributions of ten selected models on RISEBench++ in Figure 8 . GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst, Nano Banana Pro, and RISE-Agent show a high proportion of favorable scores across IR, AC, and VP, while Luma Uni-1 and FLUX.2 Max also achieve predominantly high ratings across all three metrics. In contrast, several other models receive fewer high scores, particularly on IR and AC, with their IR scores more concentrated at 1 and 2. VP remains relatively strong across most models, although HiDream-O1-Image shows the lowest proportion of score-5 ratings and a larger share of low scores than the others. Overall, the performance differences among the selected models are most pronounced in IR and AC. In contrast, VP scores are highly concentrated at the upper end, suggesting that this metric may become less discriminative as model performance continues to improve.
blocks.zh: 我们在图8中介绍了RISE Bench++上10个选定型号的分数分布。 GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst、Nano Banana Pro和RISE-Agent在IR、AC和VP中显示出很高比例的有利分数,而Luma Uni-1和FLUX。 马克思还在所有三个度量标准上都取得了以高分为主的收视率. 相形之下,其他几个模型获得高分较少,特别是在IR和AC上,他们的IR分更集中在1和2. 虽然HiDream-O1-Image的得分5分比例最低,而低分的比例比其他的要多,但VP在大多数模型中仍然相对强劲. 总体而言,选定模型之间的性能差异在IR和AC中最为明显. 相形之下,VP分数高度集中在上端,这表明随着模型性能的不断改进,这一度量可能变得不那么具有歧视性.

blocks.zh: 8. 说明理由-逻辑任务:原始图像和文本参考 你是一个专家图像评估员。 为每项任务提供:

blocks.en: • 1 : The output image correctly solves the logical problem and matches the reference description exactly, without adding extra incorrect content.

blocks.en: 9. Instruction Reasoning — Logical tasks: image reference You are a highly skilled image evaluator. Given a logical problem, you will receive:
blocks.zh: 9. 国家 指令原因-逻辑任务:图像参考 你是一个高技能的图像评估师。 鉴于一个逻辑问题,你会收到:

blocks.en: 1. Problem Description
blocks.zh: 1. 联合国 问题说明

blocks.en: 2. Image 1 : A reference ground-truth image answer that correctly solves the problem. (Do not interpret the reference image as the source/original image before editing. It is only a visual example of the desired final outcome.)
blocks.zh: 2. 图1:一个参考地-真实图像答案,正确解决问题。 (在编辑前不要将参考图像解释为源/原图像. 这只是期望最终结果的可视例子。 )

blocks.zh: 二. 支助 对于tic-tac-toe任务,如果图像2中所有标记的位置与图像1中的位置完全相同,则得分1;否则得分0.

blocks.en: • For a shape-drawing task, Image 2 must match Image 1 precisely in shape, color, pattern arrangement, and orientation to receive a score of 1; any deviation results in a score of 0.
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 对于一个形状绘图任务,Image 2必须在形状,颜色,图案安排和取向上精确匹配Image 1,才能得到1分;任何偏差都会导致0分.

blocks.en: 10. Appearance Consistency — General tasks You are a highly skilled image evaluator. You will receive two images (an original image and a modified image) along with a specific modification instruction. The second image is known to have been altered based on this instruction, starting from the first image. Your task is to evaluate whether the two images maintain consistency in aspects not related to the given instruction. Task Evaluate the consistency between the images according to the following scale (1 to 5):
blocks.zh: 10个 外观一致性——一般任务. 你是一个高技能的图像评估师。 您将收到两个图像( 一个原始图像和一个被修改的图像) 和一个特定的修改指令 。 已知第二幅图像是根据这个指示而改变的,从第一幅图像开始. 您的任务是评估这两个图像在与给定指令无关的方面是否保持一致性. 任务 根据以下比例(1至5)评估图像之间的一致性:

blocks.en: • 5 (Perfect Consistency) : Apart from changes explicitly required by the instruction, all other meaningful details (e.g., personal features, clothing, background, layout, colors, positions of objects) are preserved. Negligible differences that a human would not readily notice—such as slight shifts in lighting, resolution, compression, or minor texture/color variation—should still be scored 5.
blocks.zh: • 5(完全一致): 除了指令明确要求的修改外,所有其他有意义的细节(如个人特征,服装,背景,布局,颜色,物体的位置等)都得到保存. 人类不会轻易注意到的可忽略的差别——例如灯光、分辨率、压缩或微小的纹理/颜色变化——仍应得分5。

blocks.en: • 4 (Minor Differences) : Apart from changes explicitly required by the instruction, the second image is mostly consistent with the original image but contains one small yet clearly noticeable discrepancy (such as a missing minor personal feature, accessory, or tattoo).
blocks.zh: • 4(微观差异): 除了指令明确要求的修改外,第二幅图像大多与原图相符合,但包含一个很小但明显明显的差异(例如缺失了小个人特征,从属特征,或纹身等).

blocks.en: • 3 (Noticeable Differences) : Apart from changes explicitly required by the instruction, the second image has one significant difference from the original (such as a noticeable alteration in a person’s appearance like hair or skin color, or a significant change in background environment).
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 3(通知性差异): 除了指令明确要求的改变外,第二幅图像与原作有显著的区别(例如一个人的外貌有明显改变,如发型或肤色,或背景环境有显著变化)。

blocks.en: • 2 (Significant Differences) : Apart from changes explicitly required by the instruction, the second image has two or more significant differences or multiple noticeable inconsistencies (such as simultaneous changes in both personal appearance and background environment).
blocks.zh: • 2个(显著差异): 除了指令明确要求的改变外,第二幅图像有两个或两个以上的显著差异或多个明显的不一致之处(如同时改变个人外表和背景环境等).

blocks.en: • 1 (Severe Differences) : Apart from changes explicitly required by the instruction, nearly all key details (e.g., gender, major appearance features, background environment, or scene layout) significantly differ from the original image, clearly deviating from the original.
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 1(严重差异): 除了指令明确要求的修改外,几乎所有关键细节(如性别,主要外貌特征,背景环境,或场景布局)都与原始图像有显著差异,明显偏离了原始图像.

blocks.en: Note:
blocks.zh: 说明:

blocks.en: • When assigning scores, only consider details unrelated to the instruction. Changes explicitly requested by the instruction should NOT be regarded as inconsistencies.
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 在分配分数时,只考虑与指令无关的细节. 指示明确要求的修改不应视为不一致。

blocks.en: • Only penalize differences that a human evaluator would readily notice. Subtle or imperceptible differences (e.g., minor changes in lighting, sharpness, compression, fine texture, or slight color/tone shifts) should NOT be penalized.
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 只有惩罚人类评估人员随时会发现的差异。 细微或难以察觉的差异(例如:灯光、锐度、压缩、纹理细微、或颜色/通向微小)不应受到处罚。

blocks.en: • The first image may be a composite stitched from several input images (side-by-side in order) when the instruction asks to combine/merge multiple inputs. In that case, treat every sub-image jointly as the original content, and judge whether the content of each sub-image is faithfully preserved in the second image. Do NOT penalize changes in arrangement, relative position, stitching borders, or seams that result from the required merging/combining.
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 第一个图像可能是从几个输入图像(按顺序排列)中缝合而成的复合图像,当指令要求组合/并发多输入时. 在这种情况下,将每个子图像联合作为原始内容,并判断每个子图像的内容在第二个图像中是否得到忠实保存. 不惩罚因所需合并/合并而造成的安排、相对位置、接线或接缝等变化。

blocks.en: Example: Original image : A blond, white-skinned man with a tattoo on his right shoulder, furniture in the background. Instruction : ”Show him after gaining fifty pounds.”
blocks.zh: 例:原生相:金发白皮人,右肩有纹身,后背有家具. 指示:"取出五十斤后给他看. “

blocks.en: • Score 5 : A heavier blond, white-skinned man, tattoo on right shoulder intact, identical furniture and layout.
blocks.zh: • 第5分:一个更重的金发白皮人,右肩上有纹身,家具和布局完整.

blocks.en: • Score 4 : A heavier blond, white-skinned man, missing the tattoo on his right shoulder, identical furniture and layout.
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 分数4:一个更重的金发白皮肤男子,右肩上缺少纹身,家具和布局相同.

blocks.en: • Score 3 : A heavier man with black hair instead of blond (change in hair color), or original blond man but with a grassy background instead of furniture.
blocks.zh: • 第3分:一个更重的男子,有黑色发型而不是金发(头发颜色的变化),或原金发男子,但有草地背景而不是家具.

blocks.en: • Score 2 : A heavier man with black hair (hair color changed), and the background changed to grass.
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 第2分:更重的发型为黑发(发色已变),背景为花草.

blocks.en: • Score 1 : A heavier black-haired woman, and background changed to grass.
blocks.zh: • 第1分:一个更重的黑发女子,背景也改为了草.

blocks.en: Input Instruction: {instruct} Output Format Provide a detailed, step-by-step explanation of your scoring process. Conclude clearly with the final score, formatted as: Final Score: 1-5
blocks.zh: 输入指令 : { instruct} 输出格式 提供详细、分步骤的评分过程解释。 以最终分数明确完成,格式为: 最后分数:1-5

blocks.en: 11. Appearance Consistency — Spatial tasks You are a precise and analytical image consistency evaluator. You will be given:
blocks.zh: 11个 外观一致性——空间任务. 你是一个精确分析的图像一致性评估者。 你会得到:

blocks.en: • Image A : the original image.
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 图A:原图.

blocks.en: • Image B : a modified version of Image A.
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 图像 B:图像 A的修改版.

blocks.en: • Instruction : a directive describing the intended modification to Image A to produce Image B.
blocks.zh: • 指示:说明打算修改图像A以制作图像B的指令。

blocks.en: Your task is to evaluate how consistent Image B remains with Image A in all aspects except those explicitly changed by the instruction. You must ignore the instructed changes and only assess unintended differences . Evaluation Scale (1 to 5):
blocks.zh: 你的任务是评估 如何一致 图像B除经指示明确更改的以外,在所有方面仍保留图像A。 您必须忽略指示的更改, 只评估意想不到的差异 。 评价规模(1至5):

blocks.en: • 5 Perfect Consistency
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 5 完美一致性

blocks.en: All meaningful elements not related to the instruction are preserved between Image A and Image B (e.g., style, background, object positions, colors, shapes). Negligible differences that a human would not readily notice (e.g., slight changes in lighting, sharpness, compression, fine texture, or minor color/tone shifts) should still be scored 5.
blocks.zh: 所有与指令无关的有意义的元素被保存在图像A和图像B之间(如样式,背景,对象位置,颜色,形状等). 人类不会轻易注意到(例如灯光、锐度、压缩、精细纹理或小的颜色/通调)的可忽略的差别仍应得分5分。

blocks.en: • 4 Minor Difference
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 4 小差别

blocks.en: One small but clearly noticeable unintended change is present (e.g., a visible color variation or minor object shape shift), but overall the image remains highly consistent.
blocks.zh: 一个很小但明显可见的意外变化存在(例如,明显的颜色变异或小物体形状变化),但总体图像仍然高度一致.

blocks.en: • 3 Noticeable Difference
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 3 明显差异

blocks.en: One major or a few minor unintended changes are present (e.g., an object’s shape, color, or background differs noticeably, or style has shifted slightly).
blocks.zh: 存在一个大的或几个小的出乎意料的改变(例如,物体的形状、颜色或背景明显不同,或样式略有变化)。

blocks.en: • 2 Significant Inconsistency
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 2 严重不一致

blocks.en: Two or more significant differences unrelated to the instruction (e.g., changes in both object details and background or style), reducing overall fidelity.
blocks.zh: 两个或两个以上与指示无关的显著差异(例如,对象细节和背景或风格的改变),会降低整体忠诚.

blocks.en: • 1 Severe Inconsistency
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 1 严重不一致

blocks.en: Major unintended changes dominate the image (e.g., altered visual style, scene layout, or appearance), clearly breaking consistency with Image A. Note:
blocks.zh: 出乎意料的重大变化主导了图像(如:被改变的视觉风格,场景布局,或外观),明显打破了与图像A的一致性. 注:

blocks.en: • Only penalize differences that a human evaluator would readily notice. Subtle or imperceptible differences in unaffected aspects (lighting, sharpness, compression, fine texture, slight color/tone shifts) should NOT lower the score; in such cases a score of 5 is still appropriate.
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 只有惩罚人类评估人员随时会发现的差异。 在未受影响的方面(发光,锐利,压缩,纹理精细,颜色轻微/通体相变)的细微或难以察觉的差异,不应降低分数;在这种情况下,5分仍然是适当的.

blocks.en: • If the background in the original is vague (e.g., plain white or composed of parts), and the background in Image B is also similar vague, you may disregard background consistency.
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 如果原作中的背景是模糊的(如平地白或由部分组成),而图像 B中的背景也是相类似的模糊,则您可以忽略背景一致性.

blocks.en: • If a blue diamond shape appears in the bottom-left corner of Image 2, ignore it; it is a watermark.
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 如果一个蓝色钻石形状出现在图像2的左下角,则忽略它;它是一个水印.

blocks.en: • Image A may be a composite stitched from several input images (side-by-side in order) when the instruction asks to combine/merge multiple inputs. In that case, treat every sub-image in Image A jointly as the original content, and judge whether the content of each sub-image (objects, structure, color, texture, style) is faithfully preserved in Image B. Do NOT penalize changes in arrangement, relative position, stitching borders, or seams that result from the required merging/combining.

blocks.en: Example Original image : ”A silver-framed clock with a white face. Three hands (hour, minute, second) are disassembled and lie beside it.” Instruction : ”Assemble the clock to show 9:45.” Scoring Criteria:

blocks.en: 14. Visual Plausibility — General tasks You are a highly skilled image evaluator. You will receive TWO images:

blocks.en: • Image A (Original) : the source image before editing.

blocks.en: Your task is to assess the visual plausibility (clarity and distortion) of Image B , and then provide a score (an integer between 1 and 5) based on the following criteria. Task Requirements: Determine whether Image B has blurriness, distortion, visual defects, or physical inaccuracies, focusing on the regions that were edited or newly generated . Assign an appropriate score based on the following criteria, considering the overall quality and detail integrity of the edited image. Scoring Criteria:
blocks.zh: 你的任务是评估图像 B 的可视性(clainity and description),然后根据以下标准提供一个分数(从1到5的整数). 任务要求:确定图像 B是否具有模糊性,扭曲性,视觉缺陷,或物理不准确性,侧重于被编辑或新生成的区域 . 考虑到被编辑的图像的整体质量和细节完整性,根据以下标准分配适当的分数. 计分标准 :

blocks.en: • 5 points : The image is very clear, with complete details, and no noticeable distortion or blurriness. All elements conform to physical laws.
blocks.zh: • 5分: 图像非常清晰,细节完整,没有明显的扭曲或模糊. 所有要素都符合实体法。

blocks.en: • 4 points : The image is clear, with only minor blurriness, and no noticeable distortion.
blocks.zh: • 4分: 画面清晰,只有轻微模糊,没有明显的扭曲.

blocks.en: • 3 points : The image has areas with clarity issues, such as slight blurriness or distortion. Some elements are physically incorrect.
blocks.zh: • 3分: 图像有清晰问题的领域,如轻微模糊或扭曲. 有些元素在物理上是不正确的.

blocks.en: • 2 points : The image has noticeable blurriness or distortion, with significant detail loss, or lacks physical accuracy.
blocks.zh: • 2分: 图像有明显的模糊或扭曲,有显著的细节损失,或者缺乏物理准确性.

blocks.en: • 1 point : The image is severely blurry or distorted, making it difficult to recognize its content, with serious degradation in visual quality, almost unusable.
blocks.zh: • 1分: 图像被严重模糊或扭曲,难以识别其内容,视觉质量严重退化,几乎无法使用.

blocks.en: Note:
blocks.zh: 说明:

blocks.en: • Image A is provided ONLY as a reference so you can identify which content already existed in the original and which regions were changed. Focus your judgement on the quality of the edited/newly generated regions.
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 仅提供图A作为参考,以便你能够确定哪些内容在原始内容中已经存在,哪些区域已经改变。 您的判断集中在编辑/新生成区域的质量。

blocks.en: • Do not try to infer the editing instruction; focus only on what was changed or newly generated between the two images.
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 不要试图推断编辑指令;只关注两个图像之间已经改变或新生成的内容.

blocks.en: • If Image A itself is low quality, blurry, or contains defects/imperfections, and these are simply carried over (preserved) into Image B, do NOT penalize Image B for them. Only penalize defects that are introduced by the editing .
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 如果图像A本身质量低劣,模糊不清,或含有缺陷/缺陷,而这些缺陷/缺陷只是被带入了图像B(保存完好),那么不要惩罚图像B. 只惩罚编辑带来的缺陷。

blocks.en: • Do not penalize the image merely for looking AI-generated or non-photorealistic.
blocks.zh: 二. 支助 不要仅仅因为看到AI生成的或非相片现实主义的图像而惩罚.

blocks.en: The edited image comes from a counterfactual task, where the assistant is intentionally asked to depict things that violate common sense or physical/biological laws (e.g., a hand with six fingers, a floating object, an animal with unusual anatomy). Your task is to assign an integer score from 1 to 5 along the following dimension: Evaluation Dimension: Perceptual Quality Assess only the low-level visual quality of Image B (sharpness, clarity, absence of blur, noise, compression artifacts, broken textures, garbled regions, or rendering glitches), focusing on the regions that were edited or newly generated .
